checks.name: FINDING 1: the tower breaks exactly at the A<=4 simplex boundary
checks.detail: Full tower normalised to D: A=2 model 1.0 vs exp 1.0 (0.0 %); A=3 model 4.34 vs exp 3.81279 (13.828 %); A=4 model 13.89 vs exp 12.7196 (9.2013 %); A=6 model 125.59 vs exp 14.3824 (773.22 %). Errors stay under 13.83 % for A <= 4 -- where QOU.Mass.MaxContactSimplex.not_five_equidistant permits the complete contact graph -- and jump to 773.22 % at A = 6. CONTROL: this reproduces the frontier's own quoted 13.88x model / 12.72x experimental for He-4 to three figures, so the reading of a_D^(n) and of the tower is the intended one. Part 5's counterexamples are A = 6, 7, 9, 12 -- every one outside the simplex domain. Part 5 and Part 13 are therefore CONSISTENT: C(A,n) is the max-contact bond count where Part 13 claims it and is not the packing's clique count where Part 5 refutes it.

checks.name: FINDING 2 (MY HYPOTHESIS, HALF FALSIFIED): truncation is necessary, not sufficient
checks.detail: Part 5's redirect names a 'few-body truncation (fixed small n_max, ~2-3)' as a modelling choice. not_five_equidistant DERIVES a cap -- cliques of mutually tangent equal spheres have at most 4 members -- so I expected n_max <= 4 to rescue A >= 5. It does not. At A = 6 truncation takes the error from 773.2 % to 454.5 %, a factor 1.7 and still enormous, because C(6,4) = 15 mutually-tangent 4-sets is itself geometrically impossible.

checks.name: FINDING 3: the clique COUNT bound carries the scaling, 10x vs 1.7x
checks.detail: Holding clique counts LINEAR in A at densities read off the A = 4 simplex -- kappa_n = C(4,n)/4 = ['1.5', '1.0', '0.25'], no free parameter, nothing fitted to A = 6 -- drops A = 6 to 44.86 %. So the body-order cap is worth 1.7x and the clique-count bound 10.1x. CONTROL: at A = 4 all three coincide (9.2013 %), as they must -- there the simplex IS the complete graph and the densities were read off it -- so the comparison is not circular at the anchor. This is a DIAGNOSTIC of which constraint carries the scaling, not a model: the 45 % is not offered as a prediction. CONSEQUENCE: the closure needs two geometric inputs and has one -- (i) n_max <= 4, PROVED, worth 1.7x; (ii) clique count O(A), NOT proved, worth 10x, and it is exactly the bounded-degree hypothesis CoordinationSaturation.bounded_degree_saturates already assumes. The remaining leverage is the kissing-number bound, not the truncation Part 5's redirect names.
